During World War Two, the US almost let pigeons pilot bombs.
A psychologist named B. F. Skinner trained pigeons to peck at the image of a ship on a tiny screen.
Every peck steered the bomb: left, right.
And to avoid mistakes, each bomb carried three pigeons. They decided by vote.
In tests, the pigeons hit the target really well.
But the generals didn't take the idea seriously.
Years later, the Navy tried again, under a new name: Project Orcon.
They only gave up for good in 1953, when electronics got good enough.
So for a while, the most advanced computer in a bomb… was a pigeon.
